text:
**Short answer:** for most camping trips, pick a 250-500Wh unit, which is light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, cameras and a CPAP. If you need to run a fridge or stay out for several days, step up to about 1,000Wh.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 288Wh)
Per [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/):
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249) is their best overall. It has 288Wh of LiFePO4 and weighs 8.3 lb. The Plus has been replaced on Jackery's own site by the Explorer 300 v2, but it is still sold on Amazon and elsewhere.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199) has a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the standard version with AC outlets, not the "C300 DC."
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299) has a 600W inverter, twice the Jackery's, and can expand to 572Wh.
- **Bluetti EB3A** (~$179) is the budget pick, with a 600W inverter.

These are affiliate-driven picks. OutdoorGearLab, which buys and tests its own gear, scored the small Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) well below the bigger units. They are still fine for phones and small gear, but they are not powerhouses ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)).

## Multi-day trips, a fridge or an electric cooler (1,000Wh and up)
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top pick for off-grid camping. It weighs 39 lb, and the list price is $1,499 but it was recently under $900 on Amazon. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** (~$799) is TechRadar's camping pick. [TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations)
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** ($1,079 on sale) is WIRED's camping pick. It is IP65 water- and dust-resistant and weighs just under 40 lb. [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/)

## Best mid-range value
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was under $530 on sale and is OutdoorGearLab's best value. Its fan is noisy. [OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station)
- **Bluetti AC180** has 1,152Wh and an 1,800W inverter, and weighs about 16 kg (~35 lb). It costs $499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF, which the Dealectric page says it tested in Bluetti's cart on Oct 21. Check that the code works at checkout. [Buy at Bluetti via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) (affiliate link)

The search results only gave me a direct purchase link for the Bluetti AC180. For the other models, the review pages above have the "Check price" buttons. Prices change often, and Black Friday sales are coming, so check current prices before you buy.

**Tip:** if you use a CPAP, turn off the humidifier. It can triple the machine's power draw. [PowerStationGearLab](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)

If you tell me your gear (CPAP, fridge, number of nights) and budget, I can narrow this to one pick.
